claims.text: Prime Minister Narendra Modi held bilateral meetings with Kyrgyz President Sadyr Zhaparov and Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan ahead of the SCO summit in Bishkek.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended the opening ceremony of the World Nomad Games in Kyrgyzstan.
Formal bilateral talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping were deferred to the upcoming BRICS summit in India on September 12-13.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Armenian PM Nikol Pashinyan discussed bilateral cooperation in defence, pharma, mining, education, economic, and cultural fields.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on August 31, 2026, in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, on the sidelines of the SCO summit.
The August 31 meeting was the first top-level meeting between India and Iran since war broke out on Iran in February 2026.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged President Masoud Pezeshkian to ensure peace in West Asia and preserve freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian blamed Israel and the U.S. for the conflict and requested Prime Minister Modi to use India's extensive contacts to assist the dialogue process.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated that Iran remained committed to ceasefire agreements, but the American side failed to fulfill its commitments.

In July 2026, an Indian delegation including Bihar Governor Lt. Gen. Syed Ata Hasnain (retd.) and Minister of State Pabitra Margherita attended the funeral of slain Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi told Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek that Russia should move from endless war towards the end of war.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Vladimir Putin discussed Black Sea attacks on merchant vessels that killed at least five Indian seafarers.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin travelled together in Putin's limousine to the inaugural ceremony of the World Nomad Games.
Russian President Vladimir Putin stated that bilateral trade turnover between Russia and India grew by 2.6% in the first half of 2026.
Russian President Vladimir Putin noted that the number of Indian students studying in Russia reached almost 40,000 following a seven-fold increase over the past decade.
Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri stated after the bilateral meeting that Modi and Putin discussed addressing the growing trade imbalance between India and Russia.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi informed Russian President Vladimir Putin that India supports all efforts to end the war in Ukraine.
India's Ministry of External Affairs rejected an interim award on the Indus Waters Treaty issued by the Court of Arbitration in The Hague, calling the body illegally constituted.
The Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague stated that the Indus Waters Treaty remains fully in force and that India had no justification for suspending the pact.
The Permanent Court of Arbitration ruled that India must limit work on a hydroelectric plant under construction in Jammu and Kashmir.
The Permanent Court of Arbitration issued an interim order prohibiting India from constructing certain structures of the Ratle hydroelectric project in Jammu and Kashmir.
India placed the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance following an April 22 terror attack in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir, which killed 26 people.

Under the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty, water from the eastern rivers Beas, Ravi, and Sutlej was allocated to India, while water from the western rivers Indus, Chenab, and Jhelum was allocated to Pakistan.
Since suspending the treaty, India has accelerated work on several hydropower projects in Jammu and Kashmir, including the Ratle and Kishenganga projects.
The Court of Arbitration noted that a World Bank-appointed neutral expert will decide by July 2027 whether construction of Indian hydroelectric plants aligns with the Indus Waters Treaty.
In June, Chenab Valley Power Projects sought forest land diversion of approximately 197 hectares for the Kirthai Stage-II Hydroelectric Project on the Chenab river.
India suspended the Indus Waters Treaty in April 2025 as part of measures responding to a Pahalgam terror attack carried out by a proxy of Lashkar-e-Taiba.
Pakistan petitioned the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague in March 2026 to determine the legal status of the Indus Waters Treaty.
The Court of Arbitration prohibited India from concreting the Ratle project dam wall and power intake structure above specified levels until 90 days after the Neutral Expert's decision.
The Court of Arbitration panel evaluating the Indus Waters Treaty dispute was chaired by Sean D. Murphy of the United States.
Draft voter lists published under phase three of the Special Intensive Revision removed 6.15 crore names out of 36.08 crore electors across 16 states and 3 Union Territories.
Out of 36.08 crore electors on the rolls in the phase three revision areas, 29.93 crore names were retained in the draft rolls.
Delhi recorded the highest percentage of voter name deletions in the draft rolls at 32.78 percent.
Maharashtra saw the largest absolute reduction in voters, with 2.06 crore names removed from its draft electoral roll.
Karnataka recorded 1.07 crore voter deletions in its draft electoral list, the second highest in absolute terms.
Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy wrote to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar raising concerns over massive voter deletions.
In March, the Supreme Court unanimously upheld the constitutional validity of the Election Commission of India's Special Intensive Revision process.
In Maharashtra, draft voter rolls retained 7.7 crore voters after 21.1 percent of the state's previous voter base was excluded.
Pune district had the highest number of uncollected enumeration forms in Maharashtra at 28.6 lakh, followed by Thane at 28.5 lakh and Mumbai Suburban at 26.5 lakh.
Voters excluded from Maharashtra's draft rolls can file claims and objections through September 30 ahead of the final roll publication on November 4.
Delhi's draft voter list deleted 47.7 lakh names, reducing the national capital's electorate by about 33 percent from 1.45 crore to 97.5 lakh.
During the Special Intensive Revision in Delhi, Rohini recorded an enumeration form digitisation rate of 83.4 percent, whereas Tughlakabad recorded 52.1 percent.
Draft rolls removed more than 19 percent of registered voters in Karnataka, 16 percent in Haryana, and 10.8 percent in Andhra Pradesh.
